mainTopic: A נזיר vow made over a cup of wine (including by a drunk person), and נזירות accepted with a condition or with a misunderstanding of its laws
overview: The amud opens with a משנה: someone who is poured a cup of wine and says 'I am a נזיר from it' becomes a full נזיר. The משנה then tells of a drunk woman who said the same words, and the חכמים ruled she only meant to forbid that cup, like a קרבן. The גמרא asks how a story can contradict the rule. It answers with חסורי מיחסרא: a missing line says a drunk person is not a נזיר. He only used the word נזיר so people would stop pouring him more wine. A second משנה teaches that one who accepts נזירות 'on condition that I may drink wine and become impure from the dead' is a full נזיר. It also gives two cases of a person who misunderstood the laws of נזירות, where the חכמים and רבי שמעון disagree. רבי יהושע בן לוי says רבי שמעון also disagrees about the 'on condition' case. רבינא says he does not, because a condition against the Torah is cancelled, and a ברייתא supports רבינא. Finally, the גמרא asks why the opinions seem reversed in the משנה's last case. It answers by flipping the text, or by keeping it and explaining the difference, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A vow of נזירות made over a poured cup
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if someone is poured a cup and says 'I am a נזיר from it,' he becomes a full נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they poured someone a cup of wine and he said, 'I am a נזיר from it,' he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its basic rule: saying 'I am a נזיר from this cup' makes a person a real, full נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though he mentioned only this one cup, his words 'I am a נזיר' take full effect. He is not just forbidden from this cup; he is a נזיר in every way.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the core teaching the גמרא will discuss)
They poured (wine, usually mixed with water)
'I am hereby a נזיר,' the words that start נזירות
From it (from this cup)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If they poured him the cup [of wine],
and he said: "I am hereby a nazirite from it,"
he is a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָזְגוּ לוֹ אֶת הַכּוֹס, וְאָמַר ״הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר מִמֶּנּוּ״
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who says 'I am a נזיר from it' over a poured cup becomes a full נזיר.

steps.title: The story of the drunk woman
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells of a drunk woman who said 'I am a נזירה from it,' and the חכמים ruled she only meant to forbid the cup like a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with a woman who was drunk. They poured her a cup and she said, 'I am a נזירה from it.' The חכמים said she only meant to say, 'This cup is forbidden to me like a קרבן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story where the same words did NOT make the speaker a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים read her words as a simple vow forbidding only that cup, the way one forbids something by calling it a קרבן. This seems to clash with the rule in step 1, and the גמרא will raise that next.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident brought in the משנה
Drunk (feminine)
She intended
'It is to me like a קרבן,' a vow that forbids an object

phrases.english: An incident with a certain woman
who was drunk,
and they poured her the cup,
and she said: "I am hereby a nazirite from it."
The Sages said:
This woman did not intend
anything except to say: "It is upon me as an offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that appears to give the opposite result from step 1's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A drunk woman who said 'I am a נזירה from it' only forbade that cup, like a קרבן vow.

steps.title: How can a story contradict the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה brings a story that seems to contradict its own rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: A story that contradicts?! First you said he is a נזיר, and then you teach a story about a woman, which shows only this cup is forbidden and other wine is allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the story in step 2 seems to go against the rule in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מעשה in a משנה is supposed to support the rule before it. Here the rule says 'he is a נזיר,' but the story says the speaker is forbidden only from this cup and may drink other wine, meaning she is not a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
'A story to contradict?' A story that goes against the rule it follows
The first clause of the משנה
Apparently, this shows that
Permitted

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether the woman is a נזיר. It is asking how the משנה can place a story right after a rule when the story seems to say the opposite.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
An incident to contradict?!
You said in the first clause: he is a nazirite,
and then it teaches: An incident with a certain woman,
which shows that it is only this one that is forbidden,
but other wine is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the משנה's rule and story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The structure of the משנה: rule (step 1) followed by a story (step 2)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story should illustrate the rule, but this story gives the opposite result (not a נזיר, only this cup is forbidden).

steps.title: The משנה is missing a line about a drunk person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words: a sober person becomes a נזיר, but a drunk person does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: If they poured him a cup and he said 'I am a נזיר from it,' he is a נזיר. But if he is drunk and said 'I am a נזיר from it,' he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by filling in a missing line in the משנה about a drunk person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the rule and the story no longer clash. The first rule is about someone who is sober, and the added line is about someone who is drunk. The woman's story is an example of the drunk case.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words
And this is what it teaches
Drunk (masculine)
He is not a נזיר

steps.whyThisMatters: חסורי מיחסרא is a common tool across ש״ס: the גמרא fills in a missing clause so the משנה reads smoothly.

phrases.english: It is incomplete,
and this is what it is teaching:
If they poured him the cup,
and he said: "I am hereby a nazirite from it,"
he is a nazirite.
But if he is drunk,
phrases.notes: This line and the next are the missing words the גמרא is adding into the משנה.

phrases.english: and he said: "I am hereby a nazirite from it,"
he is not a nazirite.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule and the story are about the same kind of speaker, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is about a sober person (a נזיר), and a missing clause covers a drunk person (not a נזיר), which the story illustrates.

steps.title: Why the drunk person is not a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the drunk person is treated as if he said 'this cup is a קרבן to me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? He is like someone who said, 'It is a קרבן to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the new line and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A drunk person who already had enough wine just wants to refuse this cup. So his words are read as a vow forbidding the cup, like calling it a קרבן, and not as accepting full נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Like one who said

phrases.english: What is the reason?
He is like one who said: "It is upon me as an offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the clause added in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a drunk person's words do not create נזירות
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His intention was only to forbid the cup, like a קרבן vow.

steps.title: Then why not say it plainly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if he only meant 'this cup is a קרבן to me,' why didn't he just say that?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let him say that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason from step 5 by asking why the drunk man used the word נזיר at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he only wanted to forbid one cup, there were clear words for that. Using the word נזיר seems to show he meant real נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
Let him say so

phrases.english: And if you would say:
Let him say so?
phrases.notes: Meaning: let him just say 'this cup is a קרבן to me' instead of using the word נזיר.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the drunk man meant only a קרבן vow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that was his intent, he would have used קרבן language, not the word נזיר.

steps.title: He wanted words that would stop them from bringing more
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he used the word נזיר so people would stop offering him wine altogether.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thinks: they will bring me a different cup and bother me. Let me tell them something that is final to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the drunk man chose the word נזיר even though he only meant to refuse the cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he forbade only this cup, they would just pour him another one. Saying 'I am a נזיר' is a clear, final statement that makes everyone stop offering wine, even though he did not truly mean to take on נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: He thinks, he reasons
They will bother me
Which is final and clear to them

phrases.english: He thinks:
They will bring me another
and bother me,
so I will say to them this statement
which is final to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר: מַיְיתִין לִי אַחֲרִינָא וּמְצַעֲרִן לִי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using the word נזיר shows he meant real נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: He used the word נזיר only as a strong way to stop people from offering more wine; his real intent was just to refuse the cup.

steps.title: The woman's story now fits
steps.stepSummary: The rebuilt משנה ends with the story of the woman as an example of the drunk case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was also a story with a certain woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes reading the corrected משנה: the woman's story now supports the drunk case instead of contradicting the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נמי ('also') shows the story is an example of the line just added. The contradiction from step 3 is fully solved.

keyTerms.meaning: Also

steps.whatToRemember: A sober person who says 'I am a נזיר from this cup' is a full נזיר. A drunk person who says it is not a נזיר; he only forbade that cup, like a קרבן. He used the word נזיר just so people would stop offering him wine.

phrases.english: And there was also an incident with a certain woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rebuilt משנה begun in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story of the drunk woman illustrates the added clause that a drunk person is not a נזיר, so the משנה no longer contradicts itself.

steps.title: A נזירות vow with a condition to drink wine and become impure
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that one who accepts נזירות on condition that he may drink wine and become impure from the dead is a full נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I am a נזיר on condition that I may drink wine and become impure from the dead,' he is a נזיר and is forbidden in all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Someone tries to take on נזירות while keeping permission for things a נזיר may not do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His condition does not work. He becomes a full נזיר, and wine and impurity from the dead are both forbidden to him, along with all the other laws.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that
Become ritually impure from the dead
Forbidden in all of them (all the נזיר prohibitions)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"I am hereby a nazirite on condition
that I may drink wine
and become impure from the dead,"
he is a nazirite,
and he is forbidden in all of them.
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the things a נזיר may not do, including the two he tried to keep.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֱהֵא שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן וּמִיטַּמֵּא לְמֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a different topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition to keep drinking wine and becoming impure from the dead does not work; he is a full נזיר, forbidden in everything.

steps.title: He did not know a נזיר is forbidden to drink wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: a person who says he knew about נזירות but did not know wine is forbidden to a נזיר is still forbidden in everything. רבי שמעון permits him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I know there is such a thing as נזירות, but I did not know that a נזיר may not drink wine,' he is forbidden. רבי שמעון permits him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case where the person accepted נזירות but did not know one of its main rules. The first opinion holds him to it, and רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says his נזירות takes effect fully, even though he did not know about wine. רבי שמעון says he is not a נזיר, because he never accepted the wine prohibition, and he holds that נזירות must be accepted completely to take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The state of being a נזיר (no wine, no haircut, no contact with the dead)
Forbidden to drink wine
He is forbidden (his נזירות holds)
Permits (says the נזירות does not take effect)

phrases.english: "I know that there is such a thing as naziriteship,
but I do not know
that a nazir is forbidden to drink wine" —
he is forbidden,
phrases.notes: Meaning his נזירות holds, so wine and everything else are forbidden to him.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ נְזִירוּת, אֲבָל אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהַנָּזִיר אָסוּר בְּיַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new case of partial acceptance of נזירות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not knowing that wine is forbidden does not stop the נזירות according to the first opinion. רבי שמעון says it does not take effect.

steps.title: He knew the rules but thought the חכמים would excuse him
steps.stepSummary: A person who knew a נזיר may not drink wine, but thought the חכמים would excuse him because he needs wine to live or because he buries the dead, is permitted. רבי שמעון forbids him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I knew a נזיר may not drink wine, but I thought the חכמים would let me, because I cannot live without wine,' or 'because I bury the dead,' he is permitted. רבי שמעון forbids him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite kind of mistake. This time the person knew the rules but expected a special exemption. Here the two opinions switch sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion treats his vow as made under a false assumption, so it does not take effect. רבי שמעון says he knew exactly what a נזיר may not do and accepted it, so the נזירות holds.

keyTerms.meaning: I thought / I assumed
Buries the dead (a job that brings contact with dead bodies)
Permitted (the נזירות does not take effect)
Forbids (the נזירות holds)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the switch. In the first case the first opinion forbids and רבי שמעון permits. In this case the first opinion permits and רבי שמעון forbids.

phrases.english: "I know that a nazir is forbidden to drink wine,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל סָבוּר הָיִיתִי שֶׁחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין לִי
phrases.english: but I thought that the Sages would permit me

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין אֲנִי יָכוֹל לִחְיוֹת אֶלָּא בְּיַיִן״,
phrases.english: because I cannot live without wine,"
or "because I bury the dead" —
he is permitted,
and Rabbi Shimon forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁהַנָּזִיר אָסוּר בְּיַיִן, אֲבָל סָבוּר הָיִיתִי שֶׁחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A contrasting case in the same משנה where the opinions are reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow made while expecting an exemption does not take effect according to the first opinion. רבי שמעון says it holds.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי שמעון argue in the first clause too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון does not also disagree in the earlier case of 'I am a נזיר on condition that I may drink wine.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Let רבי שמעון also disagree in the first clause!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a challenge. רבי שמעון's view seems to apply to the earlier case too, so why is he silent there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 רבי שמעון says a person who did not accept the wine prohibition is not a נזיר. The person in the רישא (step 9) also did not accept the wine prohibition, since he made it a condition. So by the same logic רבי שמעון should say that person is not a נזיר either.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Let him disagree (a challenge: why doesn't he?)
The first clause of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
Let Rabbi Shimon also disagree in the first clause!
phrases.notes: The first clause is the case in step 9: 'I am a נזיר on condition that I may drink wine and become impure from the dead.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by comparing רבי שמעון's view in step 10 to the earlier clause in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The silence of רבי שמעון in the first clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If not accepting the wine prohibition stops the נזירות, that should be true of the 'on condition I drink wine' case too.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: he does argue there too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that רבי שמעון really does disagree in the first clause as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: רבי שמעון disagreed even in the first clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer simply accepts the challenge. רבי שמעון's argument covers the first clause too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, 'רבי שמעון permits' was meant to apply to the first clause as well. So a person who says 'I am a נזיר on condition that I drink wine' is not a נזיר at all according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: He disagreed
Even / also

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: חָלוּק הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַף בְּרֵישָׁא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon disagreed even in the first clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: חָלוּק הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַף בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by agreeing that רבי שמעון does argue.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise: the dispute extends to the first clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if רבי שמעון agreed with the first clause, since he is not mentioned there.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון argues on both clauses. A נזירות with a wine exception does not take effect according to him.

steps.title: רבינא: a condition against the Torah is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says רבי שמעון does not argue in the first clause, because there the person made a condition against the Torah, and such a condition is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: in the first clause רבי שמעון does not disagree. Why? Because he is making a condition against what is written in the Torah, and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah, his condition is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer. He explains why the first clause is different from the case in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause the person fully said 'I am a נזיר' and then added a condition that goes against the Torah's laws of a נזיר. That condition is thrown out, and the plain 'I am a נזיר' stays. So even רבי שמעון agrees he is a full נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Makes a condition against what the Torah says
His condition is cancelled (and the main statement remains)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a condition against the Torah is cancelled is a general rule used in many areas of הלכה, not only נזירות.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
In the first clause Rabbi Shimon does not disagree,
what is the reason?
Because he is making a condition
against what is written in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah —
his condition is cancelled.
phrases.notes: Only the condition falls away. His words 'I am a נזיר' still count.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: בְּרֵישָׁא לָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an answer to step 12 that is the opposite of רבי יהושע בן לוי's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a condition against the Torah is different from simply not knowing a rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases seem the same, since in both he did not accept the wine prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the first clause the condition is cancelled, so he is a full נזיר even according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: 'on condition' means 'except for'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי would answer רבינא that 'on condition' works like 'except for,' so the person never took on full נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי would say to you: this 'on condition' is like 'except for.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהושע בן לוי would respond to רבינא's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the person's words as 'I am a נזיר except for wine.' That is not taking on full נזירות and then cancelling part of the Torah. It is only taking on part of נזירות in the first place, and רבי שמעון holds partial נזירות does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Would say to you (how he would answer)
On condition that
Is like 'except for'

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר לָךְ:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi would say to you:
this "on condition" —
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't. It doesn't change the meaning.

phrases.english: is like "except for."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יהושע בן לוי against רבינא's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the person's wording so that the 'condition against the Torah' rule does not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'On condition' looks like a condition added to full נזירות, which would be cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'On condition' means 'except for,' so he only took on partial נזירות, which רבי שמעון says does not take effect.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבינא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one who says 'I am a נזיר on condition that I may drink wine and become impure from the dead' is a full נזיר, because a condition against the Torah is cancelled. This matches רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבינא: If someone said, 'I am a נזיר on condition that I may drink wine and become impure from the dead,' he is a נזיר and is forbidden in all of them, because he is making a condition against what is written in the Torah, and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah, his condition is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses exactly רבינא's reasoning for this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls the 'on condition' a real condition against the Torah, not an 'except for.' That is רבינא's reading. So the person becomes a full נזיר, with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with his view
Becomes impure from contact with the dead
Forbidden in all of them (all the נזיר prohibitions)

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא: 'I am a נזיר on condition that I drink wine' makes a full נזיר even according to רבי שמעון, because the condition is cancelled, and a ברייתא supports this. רבי יהושע בן לוי: 'on condition' means 'except for,' so רבי שמעון says it does not take effect at all.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in line with Ravina:
If he said, "I am a nazir
on condition that I may drink wine
and become impure from the dead" —
he is a nazir and is forbidden in all of them,
because he is making a condition
against what is written in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah —
his condition is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבינא's side of the dispute from steps 14 and 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that 'on condition' is a real condition against the Torah and is cancelled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that rules the person is a full נזיר for exactly this reason.

steps.title: The final case of the משנה seems to clash with the earlier case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the final case, 'I know that a נזיר is forbidden in wine.' It asks how the ruling there can fit with the earlier case, where the person is אסור and רבי שמעון permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה's last case says: 'I know that a נזיר is forbidden to drink wine.' But didn't you say in the first part that he is forbidden and רבי שמעון permits?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last case of the משנה. It points out that its ruling does not seem to line up with the ruling in the earlier case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case (step 10) the person did not even know a נזיר may not drink wine, yet the first opinion holds him bound and רבי שמעון lets him off. In the final case (step 11) he knew the rule, which should bind him at least as much. Yet there the first opinion lets him off and רבי שמעון is strict, so the גמרא asks why the opinions look flipped.

keyTerms.meaning: I know. The opening words of the final case in the משנה.
But didn't you say? This introduces a contradiction with something said earlier.
The first part (earlier clause) of the משנה.
Permits. Here it means he is not held to the נזירות.

phrases.english: "I know that a nazirite is forbidden in wine."
phrases.notes: This quotes the start of the משנה's last case. The person adds that he thought the חכמים would let him drink anyway.

phrases.english: But you said in the first clause: he is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is the earlier case, where the person said he didn't know a נזיר may not drink wine.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon permits!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ רֵישָׁא אָסוּר, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'on condition' discussion to a new question about the משנה's final case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the final case of the משנה ('I know a נזיר is forbidden in wine').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the earlier clause the person stays אסור and רבי שמעון permits. The final clause seems to reverse who is strict and who is lenient, which looks inconsistent.

steps.title: Change the final case so it matches the earlier case
steps.stepSummary: The first answer is to read the final case the same way as the first: he is אסור, and רבי שמעון permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say in the final case too: he is forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the wording of the final case so its ruling matches the earlier case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining why the two cases differ, this answer says they do not differ at all. In both, the חכמים hold the person to the נזירות and רבי שמעון lets him off. That removes the clash completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Say also. Read this clause the same way as the other one.
This person is forbidden. He is bound by the נזירות.

phrases.english: Say also:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is adjusting the wording of the final case so it reads like the first one.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה אָסוּר, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר.
phrases.english: he is forbidden, and Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the text of the משנה (reversing the opinions in the final case).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The final case has the opposite ruling from the earlier case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases have the same ruling: the person is אסור, and רבי שמעון permits.

steps.title: Keep the wording and distinguish the two cases
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: don't flip anything. The two cases are really different, and the גמרא starts to explain how ('there...').
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: really, don't reverse the opinions. There...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer. It keeps the משנה's wording and starts to explain why the two cases are different. This line is only the setup, and the explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first answer, this one leaves the opinions in the final case exactly as they are written. To do that, the גמרא must show a real difference between the earlier case and the final case. It begins that with the word 'there,' pointing back to one of the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say. This introduces a second, alternative answer.
Really, actually. It keeps the original position.
Don't reverse. Leave the opinions as written.
There. It points to the other case to show the difference.

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not finished here. The word הָתָם ('there') opens the explanation of the difference, which continues in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Actually, do not reverse.
phrases.notes: He means: don't change the final case the way the first answer did. Keep the opinions as the משנה has them.

phrases.english: There

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the step 17 question, which rejects the need for the text change in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the two cases instead of changing the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would have to reverse the opinions in the final case so it matches the earlier one.
steps.terutzMaskana: No reversal is needed, because the cases are different. The explanation of the difference begins with 'there' and continues in the next part of the text.
